title: Credit Balances Left on Earlier HomeFlood Terms
content:
**Definition.** For a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy, the credit balance left on the policy's earlier terms is their charges and refunds less their payments and credits, taken together across every term other than the installment's term, when that figure is below zero. Refunds paid out on the policy are counted with the earlier terms.

| Plan and installments still to come | Use of the earlier-term credit balance |
|---|---|
| QUARTERLY, two or more installments still to come | spread equally over them; this installment takes one equal part |
| semi-annual plan, or only one installment still to come | applied in full to the next installment |
| otherwise | refunded separately, not taken into an installment |

**Effect.** The part taken into an installment lowers the installment due by that part.

**The installment's term.** The installment's term is the term of the latest first payment (installment 1) received on the policy.

**Installments still to come.** The installments of a term are its first payment and, after it, three later installments due 3, 6 and 9 calendar months after the term start on QUARTERLY, or one later installment due 6 calendar months after the term start on the semi-annual plan. The installments still to come are those of the plan not yet received: the plan's number of installments (4 on QUARTERLY, 2 on the semi-annual plan) less the payments received for the term.

## Hypothetical cases

- **QUARTERLY, spread.** The earlier terms show 1,000.00 charged and 1,060.00 paid and credited, which is 60.00 below zero. With three installments still to come, this installment takes 20.00.
- **Semi-annual.** The same 60.00 is applied in full to the next installment.
- **No credit balance.** Earlier terms netting to zero or more leave nothing to apply.
